issue_context.title: PSSessions with Containers throw NullReferenceException
issue_context.body:
Cmdlets that deal with PSSessions created on ContainerId throw a NullReferenceException when creating the session. This is true for `New-PSSession`, `Enter-PSSession` and `Invoke-Command`, among maybe others.

The stack trace is this:
````
Object reference not set to an instance of an object.
   at System.Management.Automation.Runspaces.ContainerProcess.GetContainerProperties()
   at Microsoft.PowerShell.Commands.PSExecutionCmdlet.CreateHelpersForSpecifiedContainerSession()
````

For me the line that fails is inside `GetContainerPropertiesInternal` of the class `System.Management.Automation.Runspaces.ContainerProcess` in `System.Management.Automation.dll`.

`ContainerObRoot = (string) computeSystemPropertiesType.GetProperty("ObRoot").GetValue(obj);`

## Steps to reproduce

To reproduce this a running container is required.

```powershell
New-PSSession -ContainerId <TheContainerId> -RunAsAdministrator
```

## Expected behavior

An instance of `PSSession` should be created.

## Actual behavior

A NullReferenceException is thrown.

## Environment data

<!-- provide the output of $PSVersionTable -->

```none
Name                           Value
----                           -----
PSVersion                      7.0.3
PSEdition                      Core
GitCommitId                    7.0.3
OS                             Microsoft Windows 10.0.18363
Platform                       Win32NT
PSCompatibleVersions           {1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0…}
PSRemotingProtocolVersion      2.3
SerializationVersion           1.1.0.1
WSManStackVersion              3.0
```
comments: /cc @PaulHigin Have you any thoughts about the issue?

Yes, there have been some cases where container images do not contain the correct Hyper-V binaries needed for a PowerShellDirect connection.  The Hyper-V team who owns these binaries are aware of the issue.  But this problem is outside of PowerShell.
This issue has been marked as external and has not had any activity for **1 day**. It has been be closed for housekeeping purposes.

I am not sure on this @PaulHigin. How is this outside of PowerShell? The same container can be accessed without problems through a `New-PSSession` from PowerShell 5.1. It does look like a PS6/7+ problem to me, no?

The original issue description did not mention this.  If WindowsPowerShell can connect to the same container using the same command:

```powershell
New-PSSession -ContainerId <TheContainerId> -RunAsAdministrator
```

Then that would indicate a client error.  But I am not aware of any changes to this code in either WindowsPowerShell or PowerShell core.

The only change I see in this code was made two years ago, to fix an incompatibility.

PR #7883

/cc @SteveL-MSFT

> If WindowsPowerShell can connect to the same container

Sorry, you're right: I did not mention it in the original description. But PS 5.1 is definitely able to access the same identical container. PS 7.0.0 and PS 7.0.3 can not.
@SteveL-MSFT  Can you look at this and see if it is related to the fix you made for #7883?
Following-up with Hyper-V team to see if they have changed their schema again as the code is trying to get Hyper-V properties, but `ObRoot` property is returning null.
The official answer from Hyper-V team is that they also changed this to a field from a property.

:tada:This issue was addressed in #13375, which has now been successfully released as `v7.1.0-preview.7`.:tada:

Handy links:
* [Release Notes](https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/releases/tag/v7.1.0-preview.7)
